parts.title: Coxhead Motorhomes
parts.transcript: Part 1. Woman hires a motorhome from Coxhead Motorhomes (Dave Sparrow). Recommended 'two berth end kitchen', £545-£755/week. Damage deposit for a driver aged 24 = £460 (£250 for 26+) (1 460). Extra drivers are free (2 extra). International driving licence is fine (3 international). All vehicles under 30 months; gearboxes all manual (4 manual). Pets allowed if looked after (5 pets). Facilities: cooking incl. a fridge + microwave (6 fridge); a television new this year (7 television); sat nav; a bicycle rack (8 bicycle); mains hook-up or hire a generator £50/wk (9 generator). Nearest station Grateley, spelled G-R-A-T-E-L-E-Y, free pick-up (10 Grateley).

parts.transcript: Part 3. Tutor and Lara on multinational companies. In different markets a chocolate brand has different proportions of ingredients (21 A). Lara criticises some multinationals for replacing local managers (24 C). She wants to read about centralisation in distribution (25 C). parts.title: Soundscapes
parts.transcript: Part 4. Lecture on soundscapes. Term first used by Canadian Murray Schafer, a well-known composer (31). The soundscape is not just noise but has meaning which can be interpreted (32). Divisions: biophony from living organisms e.g. frogs (33); geophony from non-biological forces e.g. rain (34); anthrophony from humans. Bernie Krause's conclusions: every sound in nature has a unique signature (35); natural sounds are harmonious in loudness and frequency (36). Soundscape changes can indicate a change in the climate of an environment (37) and warn of different types of pollution e.g. insecticides (38). Acoustic recorders produce data used to create maps in 3-D (39). Noisiest creature is probably a kind of shrimp living in the ocean (40).
